cases.title: Use a short spoken phrase as a tempo cue
cases.coaching_finding: Source discusses tempo as a learned priority, without diagnosing rushed timing or another fault in the demonstrator.
cases.coach_reasoning: Audio speaker says a simple familiar phrase helped encode rhythm during learning. No force or kinematic explanation is provided.

intervention.application: Use the short phrase as a rhythm reminder during rehearsal; the video pairs its two parts with swing motion.
intervention.limits: The source does not prescribe fixed seconds, a ratio, exact phase boundary or syllable-to-impact timing. Any precise mapping would be an additional design choice.

applicability: Golfer benefits from a simple rhythm cue and can test it without adding several mechanical thoughts.
A tempo task is appropriate to the golfer's current priority; the source offers no diagnostic threshold.
unknowns: Original audio interview and complete attribution beyond uploader's Nelly reference.
Natural-versus-edited playback timing and whether first passage is a rehearsal or shot.
Ideal individual tempo, retention and actual strike/flight response.
cases.observed_result: Illustrative swing passages and held finish; no measured before/after or scoring evidence.

selection.policy_origin: User one-focus preference; select a single rhythm cue rather than stack technical instructions.
selection.reassess: Proposed app check: compare comfort, repeatability and real strike outcomes with and without phrase. Measure timing only from suitable unedited capture.

limits: ASR estimates for source alignment, not an ideal rhythm or backswing/downswing ratio.

source_ambiguities.issue: Original audio attribution rests on creator text, not independent identification of voice or face.
Two visual swing passages are shown; source does not establish whether both are shots or whether footage timing is unmodified.

cross_source_links.explanation: Patience/later-power and the Coca-Cola mnemonic are different possible attention cues. Select one for the golfer; do not infer they encode an identical mechanical timing change.

cross_source_links.relation: Simple feel must still transfer to target execution
cross_source_links.explanation: Ruffels distinguishes useful sensation from technical overload in target practice. A rhythm phrase can be tested as one sensation, but this montage supplies no target-transfer evidence.

annotation_opportunities: Align the original phrase audio with source motion for illustration, explicitly avoiding an ideal-timing claim.
Label rehearsal versus actual shot only when ball/impact evidence supports it.
Offer a single short rhythm cue with a later outcome check.
excluded_material: A prescribed3:1 ratio, exact BPM or universal swing duration.
Guaranteed improved tempo, strike or scoring.
Two visually successful swings counted as measured improvement.

independent_validation.reason: Mnemonic illustrated by edited footage; no diagnosis, unedited timing validation or outcome comparison.
